transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for fitting me in. Um, I hope I'm answering this right, but... I guess I'm here because work has been a little bit of a struggle lately. 

I'm an auditor, and usually I'm very efficient, I promise. But recently, I've just gotten so... slowed down. It's actually a little embarrassing to admit, but I can sit there staring at one audit workpaper for, like, twenty minutes before I even move my hand to type. It's just taking me longer to do things, and... well, people at work have started noticing that I'm not keeping up. I really don't want them to think I'm slacking off or doing a bad job, because I'm trying so hard to push through it. 

Is that... is that the kind of thing you need to know?
Have you noticed any loss of interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy, like hobbies or activities outside of work?

Um, well... I guess maybe a little bit? I hope that's okay to say. I don't want to sound like I'm just complaining, because I know I have a good life. 

But, um, I used to do a lot of things on the weekends. I'd plan these big hikes, take my camera out for photos, do a bunch of meal prep and cooking on Sundays, and I even volunteered at the local library. I always liked being busy and helpful, you know? But lately... I don't know, it's silly, but those things just feel like... like items on a checklist that I just don't care enough to start. I mean, I know I *should* be doing them, and I feel terrible that I haven't been volunteering. I really hope the library isn't mad at me. 

Is that... does that answer your question, Doctor? I just haven't had the energy to be the person I usually am, I suppose.
Have you been feeling more tired or lacking energy lately, even when you haven’t been doing much physically or mentally demanding?

Um, yes. Actually, yes, quite a bit. I hope it doesn't sound like I'm just being lazy, I promise I'm not. But... I don't know, it's like, even if I've been in bed all night, I wake up and my body just feels... well, it feels like I've been up closing an audit for three days straight. 

It's really embarrassing, honestly. Just doing simple things, like... like taking a shower, or sorting through some basic insurance paperwork at home, it just completely wipes me out. I feel awful even admitting that because I know I should be able to handle those things easily. 

I'm trying my best to push past it, I really am. Is it... is it normal to feel that exhausted when you haven't really done anything? I hope I'm explaining this right.
Have you been feeling down, depressed, or hopeless most of the day, nearly every day, for the past couple of weeks?

Um... I really hate to sound ungrateful, because I know I have so much to be thankful for. I don't want to be a downer or anything. But... yes, I suppose I have been feeling a bit down lately. 

It's just... well, most days I wake up and there's this... this heavy, hollow feeling right in my chest. It almost feels like the day is already lost before I've even managed to get out of bed. I try so hard to just shake it off and put on a brave face so I don't bother anyone at work or make anyone worry. I feel terrible even admitting it out loud, honestly, because I know I should just be able to snap out of it. 

Is it... is it helpful for you to know that? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of answers, Doctor.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight recently—like eating much less or much more than usual?

Um, well... I hope it doesn't sound like I'm complaining about my body or anything. I know some people would be happy about this, but... I guess I have noticed a little bit of a change? 

I just haven't really been hungry. Food has mostly become something I just... I force down, because I know I should eat to keep my strength up. I don't want to make anyone worry by skipping meals, so I try my best. But, um, I have noticed that my work skirts have gotten pretty loose lately, even though I'm definitely not trying to lose weight or anything like that. 

I feel bad that I haven't been taking better care of myself in that way. I hope that's the kind of information you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm being helpful.
Have you been feeling guilty or like you're not living up to your own or others' expectations more often lately?

Um, well... I mean, I try really hard to be a good employee and a good person. I always want to pull my own weight, you know? But... I don't know, I guess I haven't really been feeling like a burden or anything like that. 

I mean, I know I've been a little slow at work lately, and I feel bad about that, but I don't think I'm letting anyone down in a major way. At least, I really hope I'm not. I try to make sure everything gets done so nobody else has to pick up my slack. 

Does that... does that answer your question, Doctor? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
Have you noticed that you're moving more slowly than usual, or maybe fidgeting and unable to sit still, especially when you're feeling down?

Um... I really hope I'm not making too big a deal out of this, because I know everyone gets tired sometimes. I don't want to sound like I'm making excuses for my performance or anything. But... yes, I suppose I have been a bit slower lately. 

It's actually kind of why I decided to come in. I've just gotten so... slowed down. I'll be sitting at my desk, looking at an audit workpaper, and I'll realize twenty minutes have gone by before I've even moved my hand to type a single number. I try so hard to push through it so I don't hold up the rest of the team, but people at work have actually started noticing that I'm not keeping up like I usually do. 

I feel so awful about it, honestly, because I really pride myself on being efficient. I hope it's okay that I shared that? I just want to be completely honest with you so you have all the right information.
Have you found that you don’t enjoy or care about almost any activities, even ones you used to really like, most of the time?

Um... I really hope it doesn't sound like I'm just being lazy, or like I don't appreciate having free time. I know I should be keeping busy and doing things, but... yes, I guess I have noticed a change there, too. 

I used to be pretty active outside of work. I would plan out these nice weekend hikes, take my camera to do some photography, and I always used to cook a big meal on Sundays. I even volunteered at the local library. But lately... I don't know, I just can't seem to find the spark for them anymore. 

Instead of being fun, all those things just feel like... like extra items on a checklist. And I feel so guilty admitting this, but I just don't care enough to even start them right now. 

I'm really trying to get back into it, I promise, because I know how important it is to be well-rounded. Does... does that make sense? I hope I'm answering your question the right way.
Have you ever experienced a period of time before this one—lasting at least a couple of weeks—where you felt down, lost interest in things, or had similar struggles with energy and motivation?

Um, no... I don't think so. I mean, I really hope I'm remembering correctly, because I want to give you the right history. But... no, I've always been a pretty steady person. 

I mean, everyone has a bad week here and there, right? Like during tax season, when things get really stressful, I might feel a little drained for a few days. But it's never been like this, where it drags on for weeks and I just can't seem to snap out of it. I've always been able to just push through and get my work done before. 

This is... this is really the first time I've ever felt this stuck. I hope it's okay that I don't have any past examples to give you? I just want to make sure I'm being accurate.
Have you ever had an episode of depression before this one that lasted at least two weeks, where you felt down or lost interest in things?

Um... didn't we just... I mean, I don't want to sound like I'm questioning you, I'm sure you have a good reason for asking again. But, um, no, I really haven't. 

Like I said, I've always been pretty reliable and steady. I've never had a period like this before where it lasted for weeks and I couldn't just, you know, work through it. This is definitely the first time. 

I really hope I'm explaining things clearly enough for you. Is there something specific you're looking for that I'm maybe missing? I just want to be as helpful as possible.
